newsitem.title: LATVIA: LATVIA-SHKELE HOPES REFORMS WILL CONTINUE.
newsitem.headline: LATVIA-SHKELE HOPES REFORMS WILL CONTINUE.

text.p: Prime Minister Andris Shkele, who earlier announced that he will quit next week, said he hoped the reforms pursued under his government would carry on.
Shkele said he would resign amid increasingly bitter rows with government parties and several ministerial resignations.

"I hope that the work succesfully begun, especially in getting the basic things in order, will be thoroughly continued by the parties, and the economy will be strengthened," Shkele told a news conference.
He said that he had informed President Guntis Ulmanis of his decision and that the president, who has said he wanted Shkele to remain as premier, was unhappy.
Shkele also said the next prime minister would come from a political party although he did not name any names.
"One thing is clear, it will be a party politician. I think it could be from the big three," he said, meaning the Democratic Party Saimnieks, Latvia's Way and Fatherland and Freedom.
Shkele also said he was against calling new elections.

"There is a possibility for the parties, provided they indeed want to serve the peoples' interests to agree on a prime minister with which all of them are satisfied and to continue work of the present Saeima (parliament)," he said.
"I have always said that (dismissing parliament) is not the best solution," he added.
Shkele said he would return to the world of big business.

"I will definitely return to private business. Latvian entrepreneurs have lot of opportunities and much to do in order to find a place for their producrts on the EU market and regain their lost positions in the CIS," he said.
